source.title: MONA: Muon Optimizer with Nesterov Acceleration for Scalable Language Model Training
source.authors: Jia-Cheng Li; Jian-Chao Tan; Hong-Tao Xu; Jiaqi Zhang; Yi-Fan Lu; Ye-Rui Sun; Yu-Chen Xie; Xun-Liang Cai

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices. It contains apparent inconsistencies in stated model scales and a table summary; these are recorded only where relevant and not resolved.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests an optimizer change and reports validation loss and sharpness outcomes, but its measured claims concern large-scale language-model optimization, not the specified generalization versions. Its sharpness comparison is explicitly qualified as comparable or slightly lower, so it refines rather than establishes the mapped sharpness–generalization relationship.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on held-out validation domains and benchmark evaluations, plus SAM sharpness. These results bear on V4's optimizer comparison only in an extension setting, and on V7 only as a sharpness measurement; it does not report train–test generalization gaps or the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7. The cited optimizer and large-batch findings are prior work, not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests MONA's optimization performance, but none of V1–V8. V4 requires an adaptive-optimizer comparison with SGD or momentum SGD, or a test of its specified tuning or recovery conditions; MONA versus Muon and AdamW does not provide that comparison. V7 requires magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance related to train–test gaps; the study instead measures unscaled, gradient-direction SAM sharpness without generalization gaps. Its discussion of large batches includes no batch-size intervention.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they claim MONA improves convergence and downstream performance over Muon and AdamW across MoE scales, with better code adaptation after SFT and comparable or slightly lower SAM sharpness. Their conclusion also emphasizes MONA-Lite's approximately 75% reduction in extra memory. These are author claims; the tables show task-specific exceptions, and the sharpness results do not establish a generalization-gap relationship.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces MONA, adding an EMA of gradient differences before Muon's momentum and orthogonalization pipeline; compares it with Muon and AdamW in MoE language-model pretraining and SFT evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by benchmark: MONA is lower than both comparators on Math (CoT) and HumanEval+, and is below Muon on several other reported tasks; Table 3 also has a Muon advantage on TorchDataEval.

fits_no_version.finding: MONA improves reported validation loss over Muon; comparisons with AdamW variants also favor MONA. Benchmark outcomes vary by task, with higher reported averages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Curvature-aware acceleration added before Muon orthogonalization improves MoE language-model optimization and some held-out task scores under the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: MONA-pretrained checkpoints achieve lower code-SFT training loss and higher post-SFT scores than Muon-pretrained checkpoints on six of seven tasks; both use Adam during SFT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining optimizer choice affects subsequent adaptation under a common SFT procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: MONA's gradient-direction SAM sharpness equals Muon's at initialization, is higher at step 1000, and is lower at the other reported checkpoints.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MONA and Muon yield comparable local loss increases under a fixed unscaled gradient-direction perturbation during MoE pretraining.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: No train–test error gap is reported. The validation-loss results in Figures 2–5 and 7–8 provide qualitative direction but no text-readable numeric values. The paper reports mean ± std for benchmark scores but no significance tests. SAM sharpness is measured on a small training batch and is not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure or gap ranking required by V7. Table 2's Average row appears to have an unexplained extra score line.
record.rows_left_out: The text gives qualitative results for MONA-Lite in Figures 7–8, but these are optimizer-compression comparisons rather than results bearing on the tested claim versions. Detailed per-task results for the supplementary validation domains are figure-only in Figures 9–12 and are not needed for V4 coverage. No rows were omitted under the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy under the same recipe.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and their test-error trajectory.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local-connectivity interventions.
Adaptive methods versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited tuning; changes from broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching optimizers; the word-level language-model comparison.
Batch-size comparisons at fixed epoch budgets and interventions that reduce the large-batch penalty.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and removal alongside weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus train–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, including ranking against norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equal-size random removals.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both extracted V4 verdicts and the V7 tested status. All row states here concern applicability to the supplied versions, not whether the optimizer differences were observed. Table 2's apparently unexplained extra line is the HumanEval+ 3-shot result, followed by the averages; it is not an additional average line. That omitted task bears on no supplied version, so it does not require a missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance.
Width sweeps past interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.

Image-classification or language benchmark comparison under limited tuning; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay or switching; word-level language models. This paper compares MONA, Muon and AdamW on MoE language-model pretraining and downstream evaluations.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and batch-size-dependent remedies.
Dropout interventions and combinations with data augmentation or weight decay.

Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, ranking of generalization gaps across networks, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures. SAM sharpness is measured but does not directly measure the version's specified relationship.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
